title: Post-Course Portfolio: Online Quiz Platform
descriptionMarkdown:
# Online Quiz Platform

## Position in the curriculum
Post-course portfolio expansion: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone, and after (or alongside) the Authentication & User Management System, since scoring an authenticated user's attempt is this project's central requirement, not an afterthought bolted on at the end.

## Already-proven foundation
This project reuses the Authentication project's login/authorization work directly rather than reimplementing it, and applies Chapter 19's transaction discipline to a specific, easy-to-get-wrong operation: recording a scored attempt exactly once, even under a retried or duplicated submission.

## Project scope
Model `Quiz` (a set of `Question`s, each with several `Choice`s and exactly one correct choice) and `Attempt` (a user, a quiz, submitted answers, a computed score, a submission timestamp). A `POST /api/quizzes/{id}/attempts` endpoint accepts a full set of answers, computes the score server-side (never trusting a client-submitted score), and persists the attempt in one transaction. Make submission idempotent: a retried submission with an identical answer set for the same in-progress attempt must not double-score it, applying Chapter 18's idempotency-key discipline to a real endpoint. Add a `GET /api/quizzes/{id}/leaderboard` returning top scores, and enforce that a quiz's correct answers are never included in any response the client can see before submitting.

## Required evidence
- A scoring test suite covering all-correct, all-incorrect, partially-correct, and an attempt that omits an answer to one question.
- A test proving the correct-choice flag is never present in the JSON served for an unattempted quiz's questions.
- An idempotency test: submitting the identical attempt payload twice (simulating a retried request) produces one recorded attempt and one score, not two.
- A transaction rollback test: a failure while persisting the attempt's answer rows leaves no partial attempt recorded.
- An authorization test confirming a user can only view their own attempt history, not another user's, using the object-level check from the Authentication project.

## Review and completion
A reviewer retries the exact same submission request twice in quick succession (simulating a flaky network client) and expects one attempt, one score, and no error on the second call — then inspects the response payload for any question the user has not yet attempted and confirms no correct-answer data ever leaked into it.
learningObjectives: Compute and persist a score entirely server-side, never trusting a client-submitted value
Make a scored submission endpoint idempotent against a retried request
Prevent a correct-answer field from ever leaking into a response served before submission
Wrap a multi-row attempt-plus-answers write in one transaction with a verified rollback path
Reuse an existing authentication/authorization component rather than reimplementing login for a new project
